newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds close higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds close higher.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds closed higher on Thursday, but inflation-linked bonds ended lower for the first time this week, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.13 pct to 171.84
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.09 pct to 161.89
Volume was moderate at 180 million shekels.

Traders said that at the current level the market would tend to stabilise, especially now that portfolio managers have started moving money from bonds into stocks. Share prices have rallied this week, with the Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rising 1.1 percent on Thursday.

"CPI-linked bonds closed lower today for the first time this week. Inflation-linked bonds rose sharply during the last two months and today we saw some profit-taking," said Moshe Sagi, a fund manger at Israel Discount Bank.

"Unlinked bonds continue to be attractive. With yields of almost 15 percent and expectations for 1997 inflation of only nine percent, unlinked bonds still offer nice yields," said Ronen Kaufman at Nesuah Trading and Investment.
Traders said the Makams, which are also unlinked, also rose on hopes for declining inflation.

Dollar-linked bonds rose for the fifth consecutive day despite the rise of the shekel against the dollar. In the local foreign currency market on Thursday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed on at 3.2770 shekels against 3.2900 on Wednesday.
"The shekel started rising towards the end of the trading day, so it had no impact on the dollar-linked bonds. If the shekel doesn't decline on Friday these bonds will fall on Sunday," Sagi said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
